unlisted_practices: Revise and standardize fluid therapy terminology and phenotype definitions by expert consensus before using them in databases that train AI clinical decision support systems.
Replace quantity-based labels (low, normal, high) with adequacy-based terms (insufficient, optimal, excessive) when encoding blood and water volume status in AI training data.
Use ontology alignment, terminology normalization, and retrieval grounded in curated sources to mitigate terminology ambiguity in large language models.
Establish interrater reliability of proposed phenotype labels before using them to train or evaluate AI clinical decision support systems.

Validate AI clinical decision support for fluid therapy through a staged pathway: Delphi consensus and ontology development, operational definitions with interrater testing, retrospective validation, computational validation within the system, and prospective evaluation.
Qualify the term fluid balance by specifying compartmental adequacy of volume status and hydration status.
Supervise hybrid rule-based and data-driven fluid therapy AI systems with clinicians who validate and contextualize recommendations in real time.
Avoid ambiguous terms defining the control target in closed-loop or automated infusion systems, because such systems act without intervening human judgment.

screen.reason: Expert opinion and call for consensus proposing standardized clinical terminology and phenotype definitions for training AI clinical decision support systems in fluid therapy.
